text.p: China ensured a successful defence of the Sudirman Cup, the World Team Championship, with a 5-0 win over South Korea in the final on Saturday.
In a repeat of their group match on Thursday, the top seeds settled the issue by winning the first three rubbers to quash Korea's hopes of regaining the trophy they held in 1991 and 1993.

All-England Champions Liu Yong and Ge Fei were never troubled in setting the Chinese on the road to victory in the mixed doubles with a 15-7 15-8 win over Kim Dong Moon and Ra Kyung Min, but the singles were closer encounters.
Dong Jiong, the world number one, took the opening game 15-9 against Park Sung Woo before the hard-working Korean fought back.
He produced a mixture of immaculate defence and power play to lead 11-7 in the second but could not press home the advantage, Dong hitting back to win 15-9 15-11.
In the women's singles, Gong Zhichao, stepping in for world number one Ye Zhaoying who had suffered a shock defeat to Susi Susanti in the semifinal win over Indonesia, also had to stage a comeback.
Having lost the opener 2-11, Lee Joo Hyun led 7-3 in the second game before Gong, the world number two, stepped up a gear, and went on to clinch China's win 11-2 11-7.
Earlier, Malaysia gave new Danish coach, Morten Frost, cause for celebration with a 3-2 win over Germany which clinched them promotion to group one for the first time.
Ong Ewe Hock and teenager Law Pei Pei provided wins in the singles, and the Malaysian men's doubles pair of Cheah Soon Kit and Yap Kim Hock clinched victory in the final tie.
"This is a great start for me," said Frost, the first European to gain a coaching appointment in Asia.
"This was my first target when I took over three months ago, and it is wonderful to have achieved it. It is a very young, new team and I am very proud of them."
